definitions.explanation: A thick, dark soy sauce made primarily from soybeans with little or no wheat. Has a richer, mellower flavor than regular soy sauce and is favored for sashimi, glazes, and dipping sauces. Originally a byproduct of miso production in central Japan.

notes:
A traditional soy sauce of the Chūbu region (centered on Aichi, Mie, and Gifu). Its name comes from the dark liquid that pooled (たまる) at the bottom of miso barrels.

KEY CHARACTERISTICS:
- Thicker and darker than ordinary soy sauce
- Mellower, less sharp flavor
- Made with little to no wheat — often suitable for wheat-free diets
- Caramelizes well, prized for glazes and senbei coatings

- たまり{醤油|じょうゆ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{漬|つ}ける→漬ける：09861_tsukeru⟧: to marinate in tamari soy sauce

- ⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧たまり{醤油|じょうゆ}: tamari soy sauce for sashimi
